news.title: FOOTBALL - World Cup winner Emmanuel Petit believes Frank Lampard is ready for top jobs after Coventry City success
news.lede: And Petit also won 63 caps for France and lifted the World Cup and European Championships on the international stage. He scored the third goal in the 1998 FIFA World Cup final as France thrashed Brazil 3-0 on home soil in Paris. Petit played alongside Coventry boss Lampard for just over two seasons at Chelsea. And Petit believes Lampard has learned his lessons from his early struggles in management to take on a top job once again.

news.title: Gianni Infantino under pressure over new World Cup scandal after allowing ineligible player
news.lede: Gianni Infantino has come under yet more scrutiny after it emerged that FIFA knowingly allowed an ineligible player to play for DR Congo in a crucial World Cup qualifier. Congo made a mark at the World Cup in the summer, reaching the knockout stages, where they gave England a scare in a competitive 2-1 come-from-behind win for Thomas Tuchel's side in the last 32. One of their stars in that match was goalkeeper Lionel Mpasi, who has now found himself at the centre of an eligibility scandal. As first reported by The New York Times , FIFA knew that Congo hadn't completed the paperwork for Mpasi to switch his international allegiance from France to the African nation before they played, and beat, Jamaica in a World Cup qualification play-off in March.

news.title: Lionel Messi has completed football and can bid Argentina farewell with pride
news.lede: Messi says goodbye with 208 caps and a World Cup but there were times he thought his glory would never come. Not for the first time, Lionel Messi is returning to the Argentina national team. This occasion, however, will be accompanied by a sense of completion and celebration rather than obligation, as the country bids farewell to probably the greatest footballer ever. Messi will wear the Argentina shirt one last time this week for a friendly in Buenos Aires against Benin (who else?!)
